subject: Nimbus Retail — Dedicated capacity intake / scaling playbook questionnaire
messages:
From: Javier Ruiz <j.ruiz@nimbusretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Retail SRE Team <sre@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — traffic & sizing data request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and rollout controls. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our recommendation engine and need a sizing baseline to take into procurement. Can you send over your standard questionnaire for dedicated sizing? Specifically we want to capture: peak QPS, sustained concurrency, prompt/response token lengths (avg/p95), expected streaming vs non-streaming, and any guidance you use for cache hit rate assumptions.

I'll attach a sample day's traffic export from our staging cluster in a follow-up. Key constraints: our SLA requires 99th percentile response < 250ms for single-turn ranking calls; we expect heavy promotional spikes (2–3x baseline) for a few hours during launches.

Can we get a quick intake today so we can lock an internal budget estimate?

Thanks,
Javier Ruiz
CTO, Nimbus Retail

Attachments: sample_traffic_march.csv (CSV, 2.4MB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Javier Ruiz <j.ruiz@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — traffic & sizing data request

Hi Javier —

Appreciate the context. I'm attaching our Dedicated Sizing Playbook questionnaire (XLSX) which asks for the fields you mentioned plus some operational details that materially affect fleet sizing (burst patterns, percent streaming, KV cache reuse, desired warm pool, and model pinning). A few quick clarifying asks that will speed a sizing pass:

- Are ranking calls single-turn or multi-turn (do you expect history / chat context in the request)?
- Is the 99th < 250ms requirement for cold-start tolerant traffic, or only once instances are warmed?
- Do you expect per-tenant isolation (dedicated pool per region) or a shared dedicated pool for all traffic?

We can turn around a preliminary estimate once you fill the questionnaire. Jordan will propose initial fleet shapes based on the sample traffic; Dev will validate any networking/KMS requirements for Private deployment if you need VPC.

Next steps: please return the completed spreadsheet and we’ll schedule a 30-min sizing sync.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: nimbus_sizing_questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)
From: Javier Ruiz <j.ruiz@nimbusretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Retail SRE Team <sre@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — traffic & sizing data request

Rachel —

Thanks, questionnaire attached (completed). Quick answers inline:

- Ranking calls are single-turn (no chat history) for the high-QPS path; we have a smaller set of exploration chat sessions (multi-turn) but they’re < 5% of the overall volume.
- The 99th < 250ms target applies to warmed instances during normal operation — we can tolerate slightly higher latency during cold starts if needed, but want warm routing to be the common path.
- We want a shared dedicated pool per region (US) with tenant-aware request quotas — not per-tenant pools.

Traffic summary (from the attached CSV):
- Baseline sustained QPS: 1,200 RPS (ranking calls)
- Peak bursts during promotions: up to 6,000 RPS sustained for 20–45 minutes
- Average prompt length: 38 tokens
- Average generated tokens (completion): 140 tokens
- p95 total tokens per request: ~560 tokens (some long product summaries)
- Estimated 60% of calls are eligible for KV/prefix caching (high reuse in ranking path)

We also have streaming enabled on a small percentage (~10%) of long-form outputs.

Attached: completed_nimbus_questionnaire.xlsx and sample_traffic_march.csv

Let me know if you need additional telemetry (tail latency percentiles or per-endpoint QPS).

Regards,
Javier

Attachments: completed_nimbus_questionnaire.xlsx, sample_traffic_march.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: preliminary fleet sizing notes for Nimbus (do not forward)

Team — quick draft sizing thoughts based on Javier's numbers and our standard assumptions:

Summary of inputs used:
- Baseline sustained: 1,200 RPS
- Promo peak: 6,000 RPS (20–45 min windows)
- Avg tokens: 38 prompt + 140 completion; p95 total ~560 tokens
- 60% cacheable (KV/prefix) 
- 10% streaming calls

Preliminary recommendation (US region):
- Dedicated pool: 8 x A100-80GB (or 12 x A40-48GB equiv) serving Llama-2-13B-chat q4/q8 quantized variant with KV cache enabled.
- Autoscale policy: baseline warm pool of 6 workers, burst-to-12 workers with 10-minute cooldown for sustained spikes; immediate short-burst transient capacity via pre-warmed spare instances for sub-5m spikes.
- Batching: dynamic batching with 8–16 token-level parallelism assumed; effective throughput increase ~2.1x for ranked calls.
- Cache & prefix reuse: assume 60% hit -> lowers effective token compute by ~35% on ranking path.
- Observability: recommend per-route token and lat buckets plus an SLO alert on p99 latency crossing 350ms.

Estimated ballpark sustained capacity: ~6 workers to cover baseline with headroom; sizing for peaks requires 12 workers to meet p99 targets. So we recommend reserving 8 (committed) with burst pool access to 12 — gives balance of cost and headroom.

Rough monthly committed cost estimate (subject to region/hardware): $XXk–$YYk (we'll firm numbers in price proposal).

Action items:
- Rachel: confirm model family (Llama-2-13B-chat vs. custom fine-tune) and whether quantization/LoRA allowed.
- Dev: validate VPC/KMS constraints and whether we need private control plane for procurement.
- Rachel: schedule 30-min sizing sync with Nimbus and include SREs to validate spike behavior.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

(Internal note: will convert to a formal sizing doc after the sync and attach the capacity calculator.)

Date: 2026-03-24T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed intake summary & next steps — Nimbus Dedicated sizing

Hi Javier —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the questionnaire and traffic sample. Attached is a one-page intake summary that pulls the key inputs into our sizing playbook and the initial recommendation Jordan drafted. High-level summary:

- Baseline: 1,200 RPS; Promo peak up to 6,000 RPS (short windows)
- Model: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized q4/q8 suggested)
- Cache: assume 60% prefix reuse -> meaningful token cost reduction
- Fleet proposal: reserve 8 workers (A100-80GB equiv) with autoscale burst to 12 and short-burst pre-warmed pool for sub-5m spikes
- SLOs: target p99 < 350ms for warmed requests; p99 < 500ms during cold-start windows

Next steps:
1) Please confirm model variant and whether quantized inference is acceptable for your quality bar.
2) Book a 30-min sizing sync this week so Jordan can validate endpoints and we can capture any per-endpoint differences. I’ve created a HubSpot task and linked it here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/ND-7821
3) If approved, we’ll convert this to a formal Dedicated proposal with cost and contract terms (including warm-pool SLA and start-of-rollout canary plan).

Attachments: intake_summary_nimbus.pdf, nimbus_sizing_questionnaire.xlsx

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
